title: Weighted negative moment inequality
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $s$ be a finite subset of $\alpha$, and let $w,F:s\to\mathbb R$ be given, with $w_i\ge0$ for every $i\in s$ and $\sum_{i\in s}w_i=1$. Suppose $q>0$, $0\le c\le1$, and for every $z\in\mathbb R$, $|1-cz|^q\le |1+z|^q-q(1+c)z$. Set $a=\sum_{i\in s}w_iF_i$. Then $\sum_{i\in s}w_i|a-c(F_i-a)|^q\le\sum_{i\in s}w_i|F_i|^q$.
hypotheses_covered: Scalar inequality holds for every real $z$
replaced: Let $s$ be finite with weights $w_i\ge0$ summing to $1$, values $F_i\in\mathbb R$, $q>0$, and $0\le c\le1$. If $|1-cz|^q\le|1+z|^q-q(1+c)z$ for every real $z$, then with $a=\sum_{i\in s}w_iF_i$, $\sum_{i\in s}w_i|a-c(F_i-a)|^q\le\sum_{i\in s}w_i|F_i|^q$.
